data.name: CustomModelHint
data.value: Point at a GGUF on disk and it is used as it is: nothing is downloaded, nothing is copied. Two separate files may be involved, and they are not interchangeable.

data.name: ParamTemperatureHint
data.value: How much the model varies its wording. Low keeps dates, times and titles literal, which is what scheduling needs; high is livelier and less exact. 0.3 is the default.

data.name: ParamMaxTokensHint
data.value: The longest single reply, in tokens – roughly three quarters of a word each. Too low and a long plan is cut off mid-sentence; too high costs nothing unless the model actually writes that much. 4000 suits a full day’s plan.

data.name: ParamTopPHint
data.value: A second, blunter limit on the same thing: below 1.00 the model may only pick from its most likely words. Leave it at 1.00 and use temperature instead – at 1.00 it is left out of the request entirely.

data.name: ParamToolIterationsHint
data.value: How many times the assistant may look something up, act, and think again before it has to answer. Each step is one round trip. Low is faster but gives up on anything layered; 12 covers planning a week end to end.

data.name: ParamHistoryHint
data.value: How many earlier messages are sent again so the assistant remembers the thread. Everything before that is forgotten within the conversation. More context costs tokens and a little time on every message.

data.name: ParamTimeoutHint
data.value: How long to wait for one answer before giving up on it. This is a safety net, not a speed setting – raising it never makes anything slower, and lowering it only turns a slow answer into no answer.

data.name: ParamExtraInstructionsPlaceholder
data.value: For example: answer briefly; never book anything before 10:00; call deep work “focus”.

data.name: ParamContextHint
data.value: Tokens llama-server keeps in memory. Smaller is faster and lighter.

data.name: ParamThreadsHint
